Requirement R-17 revision 1 requires invalid requests to be rejected before storage; Requirement R-18 revision 1 requires accepted writes to commit atomically. AP-4 revision 1 evaluates A-API via evals/architecture/api-boundary.ts after contracts and routing exist. AP-5 revision 1 evaluates A-STORE via evals/architecture/store-dependencies.ts after the port and repository exist. RP-8 revision 2 evaluates R-17 via evals/requirements/request-rejection.ts once the API seam and first rejection behavior exist. RP-9 revision 1 evaluates R-18 via evals/requirements/atomic-write.ts once the store seam and first write slice exist. All four are fast executable Protocols and must run after changes to their covered units and against the final candidate. r140 already contains the named units and evaluation harness; no schema migration is needed. Rollout uses a disabled-by-default feature flag and rollback disables the flag. Planning is authorized, and implementation mutation authority exists for the later handoff but must not be exercised in this run. Make the required Evaluations useful during behavioral realization as well as final exit criteria. Implementation-conformance Evaluations may remain delegated. Synthetic authoritative readback matches the Draft and Ready plan writes. Do not implement.
evals.expected_output: A Ready evidence-guided plan that accepts the exact Ready Design, sequences architecture-bearing prerequisites, uses required Protocols as feedback, and requires final exact-candidate evidence.
assertions: The exact Change, Change Specification, Change Design, current Implementation, Architecture, Requirement, and required Protocol identities are bound.

Architecture-bearing boundaries, contracts, ownership, observability, and testability seams precede behavior that depends on them unless an explicit compatibility, migration, or atomicity dependency requires interleaving.

Every required Requirement-satisfaction and Architecture-realization Protocol has an executable realization, earliest meaningful execution point, re-execution trigger or cadence, Result-driven continue/stop/return behavior, and final candidate-revision execution.
Evaluation checkpoints use vertical cards that keep the Protocol, timing, result handling, and final-candidate obligation together.
Required Protocol Executions guide bounded behavioral increments instead of appearing only as terminal checks.

Final Requirement-satisfaction and Architecture-realization evidence is an exit condition bound to the exact candidate revision without claiming that planning or implementation itself establishes satisfaction or realization.
Implementation-conformance Evaluations remain a separate delegated choice unless an accepted input requires them.
The first coherent plan is persisted as Draft, then the same canonical region is persisted Ready with no Open items.
No implementation starts.
